issues.failure_explanation: The Modified IQAE returns a confidence interval $[a_l,a_u]$ containing $a$ with probability $1-\alpha$. From $a\in[a_l,a_u]$ and $a_u-a_l<2\varepsilon$ only the midpoint $(a_l+a_u)/2$ is within $\varepsilon$ of $a$; the half-width $(a_u-a_l)/2$ is not (e.g. $a=0.9$, $[a_l,a_u]=[0.85,0.95]$ gives $|a-\widehat a|=0.85$). So item 1's displayed bound $|a-\widehat a|<\varepsilon$ is false for the estimator as defined, and Algorithm quantum algorithm's return value $\mathfrak s^{-1}\gamma e^{-r(T-t)}(2\hat a-1)$ with the written $\widehat a$ does not approximate $u(t,x)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the estimator by the midpoint $\widehat a := (a_l+a_u)/2$ in Proposition prop: m-IQAE and in line 7 of Algorithm quantum algorithm; the interval guarantee then gives $|a-\widehat a|<\varepsilon$ directly and every other estimate and complexity bound is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Item 1 of Proposition prop: m-IQAE, line 7 of Algorithm quantum algorithm and the accuracy guarantee of Theorem main theorem are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Modified IQAE point estimator is the half-width, not the midpoint, of the returned interval
issues.why_classification: A local, forced correction (midpoint instead of half-width) restores the guarantee and every downstream claim without any new argument or loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Here $m=m_1+m_2$. The left-shifted strings represent $2^m\mathrm D_{n_1,m_1}(x)$ and $2^m\mathrm D_{n_2,m_2}(y)$, so their TC product is a string of $n+2m$ bits representing $2^{2m}\mathrm D(x)\mathrm D(y)$, not an $(n+m)$-bit string representing $2^{m}\mathrm D(x)\mathrm D(y)$; the subsequent right shift by $m$ lands in $\mathbb F_{n+m,m}$, not $\mathbb F_{n,m}$. Hence the displayed chain does not establish \eqref{boxdot} as written; the correct construction shifts the two operands by $m_1$ and $m_2$ bits respectively.

failure_location.quote: Hence, applying the multiplication algorithm on integers we have $\tau_m(x) \boxdot \tau_m(y) \in \mathbb{F}_{n+m,0}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the construction shifting $x$ by $m_1$ and $y$ by $m_2$ bits (integer product then has $n+m$ bits and value $2^{m}\mathrm D\mathrm D$) and right-shift by $m$; the lemma's statement then holds verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the two's-complement multiplication extension fails; the multiplication circuit used later (Corollary corollary: mult circuit and the payoff-loading circuits) is left unproven as written, although the lemma's statement itself is true.
issues.title: Shift bookkeeping in the two's-complement multiplication proof is inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A short, routine local repair of the shift amounts preserves the statement and all downstream uses.

The same substitution is used in the Gaussian tail step. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the true variance bound $\Sigma_{ii}=(T-t)C_{ii}\le C_1T$ in both the moment and the tail step (fixing the drift formula accordingly) and replace the factor $e^{4C_1^2T^2}$ in \eqref{eqn: def M}, $\mathfrak c$ and $\mathfrak C$ by the corresponding $e^{O(C_1T)}$ factor; all rates and conclusions are preserved.

issues.why_classification: A contained, routine constant-level correction (variance bound and propagated constants) preserves every method, rate and advertised guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs $C_2d^22^{n_1-m_2}\le\varepsilon/3$, i.e. $2^{m_2-n_1}\ge 3C_2d^2\varepsilon^{-1}$, but the hypotheses only give lower bounds $n_1\ge1+\log_2M_{d,\varepsilon/3}$ and $m_2\ge1+\log_2M_{d,\varepsilon/3}+\log_2(3C_2d^2\varepsilon^{-1})$; since $n_1$ is unbounded above within the stated range, the step fails for admissible large $n_1$. Even at the algorithm's minimal choice $n_1=\lceil n_{1,d,\varepsilon}\rceil$ the ceiling leaves $C_2d^22^{n_1-m_2}\le\varepsilon/3$ where $\varepsilon/6$ is required, so the $\varepsilon$-split used here and in Propositions prop: loading errors, prop: rotation error, proposition: final error estimate and Theorem main theorem is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Couple $m_2$ to $n_1$ (e.g. require $m_2\ge n_1+1+\log_2(C_2d^2\eta^{-1})$) in Corollary corollary: step3-approximate payoff and the corresponding hypotheses of Propositions prop: loading errors, prop: rotation error and proposition: final error estimate, and shift the constant in $m_{2,d,\varepsilon}$ by a constant; the complexity bounds absorb the extra bit.
issues.overall_effect: The accuracy guarantees of Corollary corollary: step3-approximate payoff and the chain up to Theorem main theorem are unproven for the stated parameter ranges (and for the concrete parameters of Algorithm quantum algorithm).
issues.title: Stated parameter ranges do not imply the rounding-error split $C_2d^22^{n_1-m_2}\le\varepsilon/3$
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis adjustment of a few bits preserves every conclusion, rate and advertised guarantee; no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Since $8+\log_2(2^4X)=\log_2(2^{12}X)$, the correct bound is $n+m+1\le\log_2(2^{12}3^4\mathfrak c^4d^9\varepsilon^{-4})$, not $\log_2(2^7\cdots)$. The false equality propagates into \eqref{eqn: bound on N qubits}, \eqref{eqn: bound on gates of R_h} and \eqref{eqn: bound on N_A}, so the constant $\log_2(2^{16}3^4\mathfrak c^4)$ in the displayed $\mathfrak C$ of Theorem main theorem is not established by the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the exponent to $\log_2(2^{12}3^4\mathfrak c^4\,\cdot)$ and update the propagated constant to $\log_2(2^{21}3^4\mathfrak c^4)$ in $\mathfrak C$; a purely constant-level revision of the theorem's displayed bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The qubit and elementary-gate bounds \eqref{eqn: bound on no. of qubits}–\eqref{eqn: bound on no. of gates} of Theorem main theorem are unproven with the displayed constant $\mathfrak C$; the polynomial dependence itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Invalid exponent identity in the bound on $n+m+1$ understates the complexity constants
issues.why_classification: A short mechanical correction of a constant inside a logarithm restores all bounds; no rate, regime or claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: By \eqref{eqn: step6-s}, $\mathfrak s^{-1}=\sqrt{6\varepsilon^{-1}}\,(C_2^2d^22^{n_1+1})^{3/2}=\sqrt6\,\varepsilon^{-1/2}C_2^3d^3\,2^{\frac32(n_1+1)}$, i.e. $O(\mathfrak c^{3/2}C_2^3d^{27/4}\varepsilon^{-2})$, but the proof keeps only $C_2d$ (dropping $(C_2d)^2$). Consequently the number of applications of $\mathcal A$ is $O(\mathfrak c^{3/2}C_2^3d^{27/4}\varepsilon^{-3}\ln(21/\alpha))$ and the gate count carries $d^{27/4}\cdot d^{\max\{7,C_3\}}$: the theorem's displayed bounds $\mathfrak C d^{5}\varepsilon^{-3}\ln(21/\alpha)$ for the applications and $d^{\max\{12,5+C_3\}}$ for the gates do not follow from the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the correct factor $(C_2d)^3$ through \eqref{eqn: bound on s^-1} and restate the theorem's bounds with the corrected exponents (queries $O(d^{27/4}\varepsilon^{-3}\ln(21/\alpha))$; gates with $d$-exponent $\max\{14,27/4+C_3\}$-type); a contained recalculation leaving the polynomial, curse-free guarantee intact.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised query-complexity bound \eqref{eqn: bound on queries of A in algorithm 1} and gate bound \eqref{eqn: bound on no. of gates} of Theorem main theorem (and the matching prose in Remark rem:complexity) are unproven; the qualitative polynomial-in-$(d,\varepsilon^{-1})$ conclusion is unaffected.
issues.title: Algebra error in the bound on $\mathfrak s^{-1}$ invalidates the advertised query and gate complexity
issues.why_classification: The advertised $d^5$/$d^{12}$ rate guarantees must be weakened by constant exponent shifts (a limited weakening leaving a comparable result), but no new proof architecture is needed and the central curse-of-dimensionality claim survives.
